name: Cornsilk
lede: Cornsilk is a very pale warm cream, best known as one of the named colors of the web's X11 set.

sections.title: A web color with older roots
sections.body:
Paterson defines *Cornsilk* as a beige colour and records it as one of the X11 colors, with the hex code #FFF8DC [1]. The name is older than the web list: Maerz and Paul's *Dictionary of Color* records it from 1927, and the ISCC-NBS system has a block for it (block 86) [2]. Its closest named neighbors in our library are [[ecru]], at a CIEDE2000 distance of 5.0, and [[light-yellow]] [2].

The books give no story for the name beyond the plain word, so its origin is undocumented.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Cornsilk is common as a painted color, thanks to its paleness. It appears in 326 of 23,781 paintings in our archive and is more common than 71% of the named colors [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light (52% of 198 paintings), and often a hidden color (42%) [3]. It is over-represented in Chinese painting, at 3.7 times the expected rate (20 of 635 paintings) [3]. As a printed word, the adjective *cornsilk* peaks in the 2010s [4]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
